title: chore(workflow): record Cycle 13 Stage 4 record and cohort reviews
body:
## Summary
Records the Cycle 13 Stage 4 (`record_review`) versioned review report, stable findings, coverage report, validation record, and workflow evidence manifest for `mech-goal-sequence-20261019` under `reviews/workflow/mech-goal-sequence-20261019/cycle-000013/stage-04/revision-0001/`.

- **Frozen review scope (`source_revision`):** `99fe4b44d78126d78041a69eeb366c52bedf0caa` (`1,105` total corpus records: `995` mapped, `110` unmapped)
- **Reviewed in Cycle 13 Stage 4:** `20` mapped records (`data/ingredients/mapped/Copper_II_sulfate_solution.yaml` through `data/ingredients/mapped/L-Glutamic_acid.yaml`, indices `320..339`)
- **Cumulative coverage across Cycles 1–13:** `499 / 1,105` records (`45.16%`; `389 / 995` mapped + `110 / 110` unmapped)
- **Findings recorded for Stage 5 (`remediate_findings`):**
  - `MIM-C13S04-001` (`important`, `grouped_remediation` -> `curation_edit`): `CHEBI:29036` (`Copper(II) sulfate solution`) and `CHEBI:63039` (`Iron(III) sulfate hydrate`) `SOLUBLE_COMPLEX` records carry bare metal-ion labels on `target` (`Cu(2+)`, `Fe(3+)`) without naming the dissociating aquo/solvated salt reaction or counterion (`SO4(2-)`) in `mechanism_summary` / `evidence_summary`.
  - `MIM-C13S04-002` (`important`, `grouped_remediation` -> `curation_edit`): `CHEBI:16015` (`L-Glutamic acid`) `CONJUGATE_ACID_BASE_EQUILIBRIUM` causal graph cites two unrelated entries (`PMID:27587446`, an astrocyte/TBI study, and `DOI:10.1016/s0168-1656(98)00084-4`) in `source_references` that are not referenced by any `competitive_interactions` edge or microbial transport/assimilation claim.
  - `MIM-C13S04-003` (`advisory`, `source_limited_defer` -> `defer_with_rationale`): 15 non-hydrated salts, elemental forms, vitamins, and amino acids in the batch lack populated `causal_graphs` due to missing curated downstream microbial transporter/assimilation PMIDs.

## Validation
- `kg_microbe_workflows validate-evidence --root . --previous reviews/workflow/mech-goal-sequence-20261019/cycle-000012/stage-05/revision-0001/evidence.yaml --required-output review_report --required-output review_findings reviews/workflow/mech-goal-sequence-20261019/cycle-000013/stage-04/revision-0001/evidence.yaml` (exit code `0`)

title: Record SSSOM generation invariant repair evidence
body:
Generator merge status: [Claw PR #683](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw/pull/683) is merged as [`d8f95e7ec5769d6c49ead59663ac67e323868b72`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw/commit/d8f95e7ec5769d6c49ead59663ac67e323868b72). The merged generator file is byte-identical to the reviewed `9294730a` generator recorded below. Existing evidence retains its original execution identities and hashes. Subsequent scientific curation is tracked separately in MIM #669, #718, #875 and #901.

This evidence companion to [Claw PR #683](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw/pull/683) records generator repairs for the 41 original native invariant failures and the independent follow-up findings [#684](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw/issues/684), [#685](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw/issues/685) and [#686](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw/issues/686).

Generator head used for the recorded run: `9294730aeb19d269899177678db87406f4251555`. Its independently re-reviewed candidate contains 2,980 rows, with zero native invariant rejects and zero GAP/ORPHAN/STALE/PREDICATE/GRADE drift. SHA-256: `9fff31e31008a4aba70de846febe9f7de07770d84e86e4e7730c9acc69fffe31`.

The follow-up retains curated local namespaces for B1 aliases with differing or mixed-case slugs. Relative to the previous repaired candidate, only sodium nitrate stock's generated alias changes from compound to ingredient; its historical validation stamp is not inherited by the new object. All 2,979 shared row payloads and all row dates remain identical. Curated primary identifiers and parent relations are preserved.

The date contract restores the native empty-date/Rule F path: mixed dated/dateless input remains diagnostic output, with every blank date routed to curator rejection. An entirely dateless set reports every affected subject and leaves existing output untouched. ASCII calendar parsing prevents malformed/full-width history entries from outranking valid dates. Native integration proves both dateless subjects are rejected by Rule F while Rule G passes.

The append-only supplement binds exact source revisions/hashes, native generation and validator receipts, all prior 41 diagnostic dispositions, the three follow-up issue outcomes, mutation evidence and independent final-code review. Earlier reports and structured reviews remain byte-identical. Current evidence: [report](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/46dc3e1b55bc4a2d992aa68b21a08cfadf54e8c8/reports/sssom_generation_repair_20261031/followup-684-686/README.md), [structured review Markdown](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/46dc3e1b55bc4a2d992aa68b21a08cfadf54e8c8/reviews/structured/20261101T001815Z-sssom-followup-684-686/review.md), [authoritative YAML](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/46dc3e1b55bc4a2d992aa68b21a08cfadf54e8c8/reviews/structured/20261101T001815Z-sssom-followup-684-686/review.yaml). Native inspection, validation, guarded save and the complete 979-bundle check pass.

Validation: MIM `just qc`, candidate native invariants, schema/prefix/CURIE checks, configured label correspondence and drift reconciliation pass. Claw's 84 focused tests, Ruff and mypy pass. The full CI-style suite passes: 6,025 passed, 377 skipped, 87.83% coverage (70% gate). Safety-module coverage passes at 76% (60% gate). The independent adversarial re-review found no new code defects. Independent evidence review of MIM head `46dc3e1b55bc4a2d992aa68b21a08cfadf54e8c8` also found no defects; it verified committed blobs, prior evidence preservation, all 141 successor input hashes and raw-file byte preservation under an alternate checkout. Adapter skips, nonblocking baseline label warnings and missing BTO/MICRO transforms remain documented.

Only review/report evidence changes in this PR. Canonical SSSOM, ingredient YAML, aggregate collections, unified mapping, pinned scientific dispositions and cycle files remain unchanged. The candidate is not promoted. PR #914 and Intel Cycle 12 work are untouched. Scientific curation for #669, #718, #875 and #901 is now tracked separately in PR #1007. This evidence-only PR does not apply those changes.

This PR remains draft for the user's final review. No merge, ready transition, branch deletion or cycle change is included.

title: feat(site): unify website features with the X-Mech catalogue
body:
## Summary

Brings the six website features that the 2026-10-25 X-Mech site review left **partial** on MediaIngredientMech up to the fleet's wave-1 unified standard. It also implements every candidate feature that the follow-up rating marked partial or missing, and three smaller findings from the same reviews. Every change is in the source that owns it: the record renderer and its templates, `schema_site.py`, the Pages builder, and the hand-maintained `docs/` pages. Two pieces of committed output were regenerated with the repository's own recipes:
- `docs/text_map.html`, with a new `just render-text-map` that re-renders from the template and the committed coordinates and recomputes no embedding or projection;
- `app/discussions/data.js`, with `just gen-discussions-data`.

No curated record, schema, embedding or vendored governance file is touched. The only workflow change adds two trigger paths to the Pages workflow, with permissions unchanged.

Pages here are built by the workflow, so record and schema pages are not committed. On a rebase nothing needs regenerating unless the text-map template changes (`just render-text-map`) or records' discussions change (`just gen-discussions-data`). The build now refuses a stale discussion index, so the second case cannot slip through.

Four commits:
- `abb0eaf6`: the six review features, the skip link, the 404 fix and the curation notice.
- `7d0d45cd`: the coordinator's follow-ups. These are Markdown-safe autolinking, site-root 404 routes, the fleet feedback template with an Edit link, a status disclosure that never claims human review, breadcrumbs, map table alternatives, the text-map repairs, the published discussion index, noscript messages, and skip links on the map pages.
- `f008d915`: two defects found in sibling ports (CultureBotAI/TraitMech#2033, CultureBotAI/DUFMech#377). A reference now ends at a closer it never opened, and the scan resumes after it. Narrow map layouts use `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so an opened table scrolls in place.
- `c5a69152`: the PR review's findings (#963 to #969): two tests strengthened so that reverts go red, a status disclosure that names each record's own curators and explains the two review-asserting quality values with a caveat, ISO 8601 dates in the export, and two Pages trigger paths.

Fixes #888, fixes #889 and fixes #890: each is fully addressed and verified below.

Fixes #963, fixes #964, fixes #965, fixes #966, fixes #967, fixes #968, fixes #969: the review's findings: #963 and #964 were addressed by `f008d915`, the others by `c5a69152`.

### Review features (all were partial)

| Key | Before (review, 2026-10-25) | Change | Test | Browser evidence (local build, 390 and 1280 px) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shareable_state` | The landing tiles linked `browser.html#status=MAPPED`, and the hash beat the query string, so `?status=UNMAPPED#status=MAPPED` reloaded as 2,611 MAPPED | The tiles link `?status=MAPPED`. The query string wins. A legacy `#status=` is read only when the query names no status, and is then dropped from the URL; any other hash is kept. | `test_query_string_state_wins_over_a_legacy_status_hash` (runs the page's own script in Node over 5 URLs), `test_landing_status_tiles_link_the_query_string_state` | The review's reproduction: choosing UNMAPPED after arriving from `#status=MAPPED`, then reloading, shows UNMAPPED, "Showing 260 of 2953". A cold load of the review's URL shows 260 and drops the hash. The tile opens with Tab and Enter. Tab reaches Sort, and type-ahead writes `sort=name-desc`. Reset clears the URL. An HTML payload in `?q=` stays text. |
| `evidence` | 85 references printed as text on 32 record pages, 5 bare Pmid rows, and 4 links ending in `)` (#888, #889) | One escaping-safe linker, applied to every free-text field #888 lists, plus discussions and dataset descriptions. A token ends at whitespace, `<`, `>` or `"`, and at the first `)`, `]` or `}` it never opened. The scan then resumes right after it, so `(https://a.example/x)-(https://b.example/y)` gives two links, while `Foo_(bar)` and `a[0]` keep their brackets. Sentence punctuation and a trailing `*` or backtick are dropped, because curation notes are Markdown (about 1,100 bold and code marks). A `pmid` slot's bare number links to PubMed. The visible text is unchanged. | `test_reference_links_stop_before_enclosing_brackets_and_punctuation` (7 cases), `test_markdown_marks_stay_out_of_reference_links` (Markdown link, bold, inline code, quotes, trailing colon), `test_references_end_at_an_unopened_closer_and_the_next_one_is_found` (two adjacent URLs, two adjacent DOIs, balanced parentheses and brackets), `test_a_pmid_slot_links_its_bare_number_to_pubmed`, `test_free_text_references_link_in_every_record_section` (8 sections, each assertion scoped to its section) | A corpus audit of all 2,953 rendered record pages finds **0** references outside a link (main: 85 on 32 pages), **0** targets ending in an unbalanced `)` (main: 4) and **0** bare Pmid rows (main: 5). The visible text of every page's main element is identical to main's build, except an added "All knowledge gaps and discussions" link on the 8 records that carry discussions. A DOM walk on 10 records finds no loose token. |
| `source_link` | Footers named the YAML as plain code | The footer links the YAML on GitHub (`blob/main`, percent-encoded), the raw file, and "Edit on GitHub". | `test_record_footer_links_its_yaml_and_a_prefilled_issue` | All 23 percent-encoded source paths (parentheses, Greek letters, ß) return HTTP 200 for both blob and raw. |
| `cross_mech_links` | "Search CultureMech" went to `CultureMech/app.html` (404) on all 2,953 pages; the PathwayMech, CMMMech and NaturalProductMech links dropped their query | CultureMech uses the verified `app/browser.html?q=` route. The other three label searches are removed. On 30 randomly drawn preferred terms they matched 0, 1 and 4 terms, while CultureMech found recipes for every sampled term whose record occurs in media. | `test_record_page_sibling_links_use_verified_routes`, `test_static_page_sibling_links_are_verified_routes_or_site_roots` | NaCl's link loads CultureMech (HTTP 200) with the query applied. Record pages now emit only the Mech directory, the CultureMech search and 5 CultureMech recipe ids, and all 5 return HTTP 200. |
| `license` | Browse, the maps and 260 schema pages had none; elsewhere it was unlinked | "Project data: CC BY 4.0. Code: BSD-3-Clause. Third-party source material keeps its own terms (licence scope)", worded from `LICENSE` and linking LICENSE-DATA, LICENSE-CODE and LICENSE. It is on every page type: landing, Browse, text map, both KG maps, records index, records, schema pages, 404 and the discussion index. | `test_every_page_type_footer_states_the_repository_licences`, `test_footer_licences_are_the_ones_the_licence_files_grant`, `test_discussion_index_is_published_with_a_way_back_and_the_licence` | The footer licence and all three links are visible on 15 pages at both widths. |
| `downloads` | The bulk files were summaries | The existing Pages build step writes `downloads/mediaingredientmech-records.jsonl.gz`: every record in full, one JSON object per line, sorted by source file, deterministic, with YAML dates and timestamps written in ISO 8601. It also writes `downloads/manifest.json` with count, bytes and SHA-256. Both are in the build receipt, and `check_site()` refuses an export that lost a record. Nothing is committed, and the build step is unchanged. The landing Downloads card links both and says they are generated at deploy time. | `test_bulk_download_holds_every_complete_record_in_source_order`, `test_site_check_refuses_an_export_that_lost_a_record`, `test_bulk_download_bytes_do_not_depend_on_build_time`, `test_bulk_download_writes_unquoted_yaml_dates_as_iso_8601`, `test_landing_downloads_card_links_the_deploy_time_export` | From the landing card: 2,953 lines, 1,319,635 bytes, SHA-256 equal to the manifest. The bytes are identical in the uv environment and in a clean CI-equivalent one. The artifact grows from 44 MB to 49 MB; no page budget is declared. |

### Candidate features (live rating `20261025T222014Z-xmech-candidate-features.json`)

| Key | Rating | Change | Test | Browser evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `skip_link` | missing | The first element on the landing, Browse, record, records index, schema, 404 and all three map pages is a skip link to `main#main-content`. | `test_landing_listing_record_and_map_pages_start_with_a_skip_link` (10 pages) | On 10 pages at both widths, the first Tab stop is the visible skip link, and Enter moves to main. |
| `not_found_page` | partial: under `records/ingredient/mapped/` all relative links and `theme-toggle.js` 404'd | Every route is site-root-absolute (`/MediaIngredientMech/…`). The page also gains a licence footer, a skip link, a Discussions link, and the OS-dark header rule it lacked. | `test_not_found_page_routes_resolve_from_any_depth` | Verified with the canary's `pages_server.py` and with this PR's own server. A missing URL at the root, one level down and three levels down returns 404, and all 11 site-root routes return 200. The toggle loads, and the search box lands on Browse with the query. |
| `feedback_route` | missing | Fleet template: an issue titled `Problem with <record id>` (the stable `MIM:` id, because identifiers are shared between records), whose body is the page URL, plus "Edit on GitHub" for the tracked YAML. | `test_record_footer_links_its_yaml_and_a_prefilled_issue` | The title and body decode correctly, and the Edit link is present, on 10 records. |
| `curation_notice` | missing | The landing footer quotes the README: an "LLM-assisted curation system for media ingredient ontology mappings" that "manages the ingredient records aggregated from media recipes in CultureMech". Record headers have a "What this status means" disclosure. It quotes the schema's status and quality descriptions, read from the schema at render time, and says how many curation events, curators and LLM-assisted events the record's own history lists. The disclosure names the record's own curators as its history records them. The schema records a curator as a "username or system", and nothing in the history marks which curators are people; three events record `curator: manual`. So the two quality values whose description asserts human review (`LLM_ASSISTED` "human-verified", and `MANUAL_CURATION` "by expert", which one record carries) are explained with the schema's words, attributed to the schema, plus a caveat that the history cannot confirm a review. The page never asserts one. | `test_record_header_quotes_the_schema_meaning_of_its_status_and_quality`, `test_status_explanation_never_claims_human_review` (parametrized over the two literal values), `test_status_explanation_names_the_records_own_curators`, `test_landing_quotes_how_the_readme_says_records_are_made` | On NaCl: "MAPPED: Has valid ontology mapping · EXACT_MATCH: Direct exact match to ontology term · The curation history lists 21 events by 13 curators (import_from_culturemech, …); 4 are marked LLM-assisted." On Atrop_Abyssomicin_C: "MANUAL_CURATION: the schema describes this value as “Manually curated by expert”. This page cannot confirm that: the curation history records each curator as a username or system, and does not say whether a person reviewed the mapping." A scan of all 2,953 disclosures finds no human or expert wording outside a quoted schema description. |
| `breadcrumbs` | partial: a site menu ending "MIM › id" | Record pages carry a trail, Home › Ingredients › `<status subset>` › record, in a `nav` labelled "Breadcrumb". Every crumb except the current page is linked, and the current page has `aria-current`. The category crumb is the record's subset of the listing (`browser.html?status=…`). The site menu is now its own navigation and gains Record Index and Discussions. | `test_record_breadcrumb_trails_home_listing_status_and_record` | Trails on 10 records, including MAPPED, REJECTED and AMBIGUOUS subsets; every crumb returns HTTP 200. |
| `visual_alternative` | partial: KG map table rows had no record links; the text map had no table | Both KG map tables render when first opened and link each row to its record, through the inspector's exact record-id lookup (now exposed by `map-record-navigation.js`). If the catalog fails, they say links are unavailable. The table sits in a named, focusable scroll region. The text map gains a "View data as table" disclosure listing all of its points with record links. | `test_map_record_lookup_is_exposed_for_the_data_tables`, `test_map_data_table_rows_link_their_records_when_opened` (both maps, run in Node), `test_text_map_page_states_coverage_and_offers_its_points_as_a_table`, `test_narrow_map_layout_is_not_widened_by_an_opened_table` | Opened by keyboard: 2,340 of 2,340 rows linked on each KG map, rendered only on open, with sample links returning 200. On the text map, 2,872 of 2,872 rows are linked. At 390 px every opened table scrolls in place and the page stays 390 px wide; before `minmax(0, 1fr)`, the text map's opened table widened it to 1,295 px. |
| `text_map` | partial: "2872 / 2872" with no word on the 81 missing records | **Also found:** 16 points (files named with parentheses, such as `(-)-anisomycin`, `Calcium(2)`) opened a 404. `embed_records.py` stored page names without the `_` the renderer keeps. The page now matches each point to the catalog the deploy publishes, by file name under either rule. That match also survives curation moving a record between `mapped/` and `unmapped/`. The page then states its coverage. `embed_records.py` now uses the renderer's page name for the next run; no embedding was re-run. | `test_text_map_points_open_the_published_record_and_coverage_is_stated` (Node; legacy-rule and current-rule names, moved and removed records), `test_text_embedding_names_the_page_the_site_publishes` | "This map plots 2,872 of the 2,953 ingredient records. 81 REJECTED records are not plotted: the text embedding leaves them out by design." A canvas click on `(-)-anisomycin` now opens its record (HTTP 200), where main's build opened a 404. |
| `discussions` | partial: records showed knowledge gaps, but no index was published | The shared claw discussion browser is published at `app/discussions/` and linked from every navigation and from each record's discussion section. Its config named an old local route (`pages/ingredient/…`), so `data.js` was regenerated with the recipe pointing at `records/ingredient/`; it differs only in those 8 links. The build adds MIM's way back and licence at fixed anchors in claw's template. It refuses an index whose discussions or links disagree with the records ("run `just gen-discussions-data`"). The Pages workflow also redeploys when `app/discussions/**` or `conf/discussions_config.yaml` changes. | `test_discussion_index_is_published_with_a_way_back_and_the_licence`, `test_build_refuses_a_discussion_index_that_does_not_match_the_records` (2 cases), `test_committed_discussion_index_matches_the_records`, `test_navigation_links_the_discussion_index`, `test_pages_redeploy_when_the_discussion_index_or_its_route_changes`; `test_discussion_preview_links.py` updated to the published layout | The index shows "8 of 8"; its back-links work, and all 8 record links return 200. The 1-Kestose record links the index. |
| `no_js_fallback` | partial: Browse said "Loading ingredients…" forever | `<noscript>` messages on Browse, the three maps and the landing counts say JavaScript is needed and point to the static Record Index. | `test_javascript_pages_point_to_the_static_index_without_it` (5 pages) | With JavaScript off, all four checked pages show the message and the link. |

### Other findings addressed
- **Landing load failure** (review finding 7): a failed or non-OK catalog load says "Counts unavailable…" in an alert with a keyboard-operable Retry. Before, a parseable HTTP error body would have read as an empty catalog. Tested by `test_landing_count_failure_is_visible_and_recoverable`.
- **Map help text** (#890): both KG maps now describe the record link they have. Tested by `test_map_help_describes_the_record_link_it_has`.
- **CURIEs:** the kg-microbe node row and the graph's component ids link their resolver.
- **Fixed theme toggle at 390 px:** it covered the last footer line on record, index, schema and text-map pages; on main it covered "Build Manifest" and "CC BY 4.0". Footers now reserve its 58 px. Tested by `test_footers_leave_room_for_the_fixed_theme_toggle`.

**Mutation check:** 76 targeted reverts, each run in a fresh pytest process with a fresh bytecode cache, and every one turned its test red. Four tests were tightened after a mutation first stayed green: the landing loader's HTTP-error branch, rejected-label sources, eager table rendering, and the noscript wording. A fifth mutation stayed green because excluding `]` from the token pattern had become redundant once the unopened-closer cut existed, so that exclusion was removed. The PR review found two more tests that stayed green under a revert (#965, #966); both now go red.

## Checks run

- `tests/test_unified_site_features.py`: 70 passed. The related existing site tests also pass. After `f008d915` the links on all 2,953 record pages are identical to the previous build's, and the reference audit still finds 0 references printed as text and 0 bad targets. After `c5a69152` only Atrop_Abyssomicin_C's links change, because its quality line now links the schema definition.
- `just test` (full suite) at `c5a69152`: **3,232 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed** (49 min). At `f008d915` it was 3,229 passed; at `7d0d45cd`, 3,222; at `abb0eaf6`, 3,197.
- `just lint`, `just format-check`, `just typecheck`: all pass.
- `just qc` at `c5a69152`, run with `CLAW_ROOT` set: **exit 0**, as it also was at `f008d915` and `7d0d45cd`. It covers validate-all, validate-strict (0 ERROR rows), qc-evidence, qc-sssom, qc-roundtrip (round trip verified; both published visualizations name only live records), qc-duplicate-ids, qc-kg-microbe-node-ids, qc-component-partonomy, qc-flat-coverage, check-instruction-refs and check-curation-targets. No tracked file was rewritten.
- `scripts/build_pages_site.py --output` and `--check`: "Built and verified 2953 public ingredient pages", "Ingredient site is complete and current".
- The `qc-flat-coverage` CI job, reproduced in a clean Python 3.13 environment with only its five packages: both steps pass, and the export is byte-identical.
- Baseline: before any edit, main's build reproduced the committed `docs/` except the catalog's wall-clock `metadata.generated`, and `docs/text_map.html` reproduced byte for byte.
- Claw `kg-microbe-site check --mech mediaingredientmech` reports "declares no site contract" (exit 0). Its `check_site()`, run directly on the build product, gives 0 findings on main and 10 here, all `BROKEN_REFERENCE` on `404.html`'s site-root routes. The checker treats the artifact directory as `/`, while Pages serves this project site under `/MediaIngredientMech/`, where all 11 routes return 200 (above). See "Left out".
- Headless Chrome (isolated profile) against the built artifact, served the way Pages serves it: **178 of 180** checks pass. The two failures are identical on main's build (see "Left out"). The only console errors are the 404 page's own status and the browser's automatic `/favicon.ico` request.

## Overlap with open PRs

- **#913:** a trial `git merge-tree` of this head conflicts only in `docs/browser.html`. Both PRs edit `applyHashFilters()` and `applyFilters()`, where the URL-state defect lives. The map, landing, justfile and Pages-workflow changes merge cleanly. #913's `docs/browser.html` diff also deletes the query-string state that #907 added. Whichever lands second should keep the query-string state.
- **#915:** it already conflicts with main in `scripts/browser_export.py`, which this PR does not touch.
- Since the branch point, main has gained #954 through #962 (#957 is this PR), all touching only `reviews/workflow/`. The branch merges cleanly with main at `baa47ca1`.

## Left out, and why

- **Landing footer link contrast, light theme:** links in the accent colour on the translucent footer band measure about 4.1:1, against the 4.5:1 required. The same is true on main for its 9 existing footer links, and the new links inherit it. Fixing it means choosing between a darker link colour and an opaque footer band, a palette call for the owner.
- **Browse heading at 390 px** overflows its own box by 2 px into the header padding. The page itself does not overflow; same on main.
- **Claw's site check and site-root paths:** the brief requires `/MediaIngredientMech/…` routes in the 404, and the claw checker has no notion of a Pages project base path, so it reports them as broken. That is a checker follow-up for any Mech that adopts the contract.
- **Discussion index theming:** claw's shared template has no dark theme or theme toggle. MIM does not edit claw's output beyond the link and footer, so theming that page belongs to claw's template.
- **A NaturalProductMech relation** for natural-product ingredients would be a new cross-Mech relation, not a repair.

title: Decide #236: a MIM: subject is the escaped file stem, and nothing re-derives it
body:
Closes #236.

## The decision

A `MIM:` subject is **`mim_curie_for_stem(<per-record file stem>)`** — fixed for the life of the record, never re-derived from `preferred_term`. Recorded in `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §2 → *Subject identifiers*.

#236 framed this as a trade-off between stable per-record paths and slug/path agreement. That trade-off only exists if the slug comes from the **label**. `FilenameIndex` never renames a file, so a subject derived from the **stem** gets both.

## It was already the rule — it just wasn't written where anyone could find it

| | |
|---|---|
| claw's publisher | `subject_id  MIM:<safe_stem>  -- stable per-YAML CURIE` |
| `CurieNormalizer` | known set built from file stems; anything else → `UNKNOWN_SUBJECT` |
| `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` | already said "Keep the SSSOM `subject_id`" — inside a blockquote about *spelling corrections* |

**Option 2 was wrong on its own terms.** A subject naming no file is not harmless: the resolver returns `UNKNOWN_SUBJECT` and `equivalent_term` refuses to cite the mapping.

## The 18 "unresolved subjects" were a checker bug

`check_sssom_subject_files.py` compared subjects against **unescaped** stems. All 18 were subjects whose stem holds `(`, `)` or `α`:

```
file '(R)-lactate.yaml'  ->  MIM:~28R~29-lactate
```

Measured with the escaping the resolver itself uses: **zero** genuine mismatches. The tool declaring the question undecided was producing the evidence that it was. It now escapes, and **gates** — in `just qc-sssom` and in the `qc-sssom` workflow.

## What still disagreed with the rule

**The mechanism #236 was filed about was still live.** `relabel_mapped_record` rewrote `cols[0] = f"MIM:{sanitize_filename(new_term)}"` on every rename while leaving the file where it was. Its own docstring names the exact record #236 cites. A relabel now changes `subject_label` only.

**`merge_salt_label_duplicates` had a trap.** It dropped `f"MIM:{lose_label.replace(' ', '_')}"`, which only matched because its three labels equal their stems. Switching to the stem needed care: the loser is rewritten to carry the **winner's** identifier before the drop, and `FilenameIndex` matches identifier first — so a lookup at that point returns the *winner's* stem and would drop the winner's rows. The stem is now captured before the rewrite, pinned by a test that demonstrates the trap directly.

| kind | sites |
|---|---|
| label-derived subject | `relabel_mapped_record`, `merge_salt_label_duplicates`, `reground_aromatic_hydrocarbon` (now refuses to guess) |
| right stem, no escape | `create_records_from_groundings`*, `add_culturemech_gap_labels`, `move_mapped_out_of_unmapped_collection`, `promote_resolved_unmapped`, `promote_microbedecoder_residual`, `promote_microbedecoder_reviewed` |
| hand-written copy of the escape rule | `validate_sssom_invariants`, `backfill_sssom_surface_forms`, `build_curie_alias_map`, `check_sssom_subject_files` |
| dead code rewriting the published SSSOM | `decompose_py_media_and_ground_categories` (removed) |

\* compared the unescaped subject against `published`, so an escape-needing stem would miss the dedupe and emit a **duplicate row**.

**Five copies of the escape rule, and three had independently rediscovered the same bug** — the validator's and backfill's docstrings both record it. The fourth copy still had it. All now call `mim_curie_for_stem`. The validator's copy said it was inlined "to keep the validator stdlib-only"; that stopped being true when Rule J added a package import, and `curie.py` is stdlib-only anyway.

**Rule B1 is unaffected.** 23 record stems need escaping; **none** publishes a narrowMatch, and the registry slug drops those characters rather than escaping them (`MIM:Synthetic_Sea_Salts_~28sss~29` ↔ `kgmicrobe.compound:synthetic_sea_salts_sss`). §2's claim that the two slugs are "always the same" is corrected to say so.

## Verification

**Canaried in CI's exact environment** — Python 3.13 with only `pyyaml`, package confirmed *not* importable — with each step's own exit code:

```
validate_published_curies.py     exit=0
validate_sssom_invariants.py     exit=0
reconcile_sssom.py               exit=0
check_sssom_subject_files.py     exit=0
```

Every guard mutation-checked by reintroducing its defect:

```
A relabel rewrites subject again       1 failed
B writer spells subject by hand        1 failed
C second copy of the escape idiom      1 failed
D merge drops a label-derived subject  1 failed
E checker back to raw stems            1 failed
restored                               13 passed
```

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `qc-sssom` (now incl. the subject gate) | OK |
| `qc-flat-coverage`, `check-unified-freshness` | OK |
| `lint` / `format-check` / `typecheck` / `check-instruction-refs` | clean |
| all 15 touched scripts import | OK |
| unused-name findings in touched scripts | 11 on main, 11 here — **none introduced** |

## A correction to my own recommendation

The inventory I gave before starting was cut short by a `head -10` and **missed `relabel_mapped_record` — the one that matters most**. The regression guard scans the whole tree rather than trusting a list.

Also worth knowing: `just lint` only checks `src/`, so unused names in `scripts/` accumulate unseen — there are 11 pre-existing in these files alone. That's #534's territory.

Full suite is running; I will confirm before asking for the merge.

title: Add fleet semantic PaCMAP and verified specialty graph maps
body:
Adds a common semantic PaCMAP for all 2,877 active ingredient records and regenerates both specialty graph views from verified KG-Microbe vectors. The text map uses the fleet's pinned BGE-large model and links every point to its exact browser record; navigation is enabled only after the complete current input and selected artifact bundle validate.

The common-map validator now rejects symbolic links for the active pointer, generation directory and manifest, and requires the selected generation name to match the canonical manifest identity (CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#440). The installed validation/staging runtime is SHA256 `9ef7708303150938c8f2c2a81885d9184ed0a7af0a78d9acc88c01224339b5fe`, from reviewed canonical candidate `16ce0e452af975cdfe4acc181efb6bad4688f5b7`. The existing numerical artifact was built with runtime SHA256 `470a3ee46db65b1ad041ead394588f3b75b53b0fb97bb62e1852827a2e7e2dc6`; that build provenance remains unchanged. A fresh full export of all 2,877 prepared records passed inspect, check and generation-bound staging with the new runtime; all three staged files exactly match the installed and previously published bundle. 38 existing focused adapter/publication/recipe tests passed after the update. The runtime commit changes only `scripts/embedding_pipeline.py`, preserves the deployed pin and all generated artifacts, and performs no new model inference, projection or site regeneration.

The graph views now project 2,212 records and explicitly report the 665 without matching vectors. They remove implicit synthetic centroids, preserve matching-method coverage, and bind the parsed source bytes, current corpus, ordered matrix, actual PaCMAP/sfdp reducer and published outputs in checksum receipts. The browser verifies those receipts and presents accurate coverage and matching explanations. Both specialty views remain available alongside the common map. A lightweight publication preflight independently binds both graph receipts to every current mapped/unmapped YAML file, including ignored and rejected records. Pages runs it before any site writes or upload; local `build-docs` and `check-visualizations` run it first. A notes-only MediaDive source correction now refuses stale graph publication even when the common text input is unchanged. Ordinary CI never regenerates vectors or layouts.

Validation:

- Full repository suite after #684: 2,483 passed, 6 skipped; package coverage gate and advisory scripts report passed. Flat-export publication coverage passed during the earlier complete integration review.
- Final formatting, Ruff and mypy gates passed; 37 focused common-map adapter/site/recipe tests passed.
- Full common-map input/cache/bundle checks and all 2,877 browser destinations passed. Both complete specialty maps passed source/corpus/output receipt checks, finite-coordinate checks and browser provenance tests; adversarial checksum, cache, publication-binding and quoted-argument controls passed independent review.
- The #684 gate passed against both complete 2,212-point graphs and all 2,951 current YAML files using only the standard library. Its 43 focused tests passed; fresh-process corpus, local-order and workflow-trigger mutation controls each passed green/red/green.
- The complete semantic JSONL remained byte-identical after the typing fixes. Main's data tree remained unchanged at the final release preflight.
- All new canonical files passed governance plan/apply/check against reviewed CLAW commit `dbac7ddc8f1351493b90c6dc8850319769fdf620`; the unchanged deployed pin still validates all 16 currently governed files.

This is the additive fleet bootstrap in the reviewed release plan. It deliberately retains main's exact `c8b8f89ecf29574d7e24f6c65cfd925aefbdd007` pin. After every consumer has the new files and CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#432 lands, a separate follow-up will pin its actual main-reachable merge commit, with artifact bytes verified against the reviewed source. This draft does not request a merge before that coordinated review.

Fixes #678. Fixes #679. Fixes #680. Fixes #681. Fixes #682. Fixes #684.
Related: CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#426, CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#429, CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#430, CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#434.
